prompt:
Write the appraiser's remarks (about 80 words) on a body shop repair estimate after a low-speed head-on collision. Describe the damage seen on the vehicle and the repair plan. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1433; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- Two similar charges on the same day are being checked.
- The repair labor hours are a little high for this damage.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
text: The front bumper cover is cracked across the center and the radiator support is bent, which fits the low-speed frontal impact described. The hood latch and both headlamp assemblies show crush marks consistent with the same event. Most of the damage lines up well with the reported collision. Two similar charges posted on the same day are still being reviewed against the parts invoices. The labor hours look a little high for this scope of work and should be checked against the standard repair times. No prior damage to the vehicle is known. Recommended plan: replace the bumper cover, radiator support, hood latch and both headlamps, then align and test the cooling system.
